Join us at The Agent Arena Hackathon hosted by Vultr to build what the next generation of agent infrastructure actually looks like in production.

Agents are writing code, driving browsers, and running real operations for teams. The infrastructure built to contain and coordinate what they do needs to get better.

Vultr is bringing the tools for you to build infrastructure powering the next generation of autonomous execution: VM backends, serverless inference, and the compute layer agents run on when they stop talking and start acting.

Compete for more than $10,000 across cash and credits!

Note: This event is fully in-person in San Francisco. Teams may have up to four members. All attendees must apply and be approved. Submitting an application does not guarantee a seat; approved applicants must confirm their attendance.

​Build, deploy, and scale with Runpod—from anywhere.

​From October 23 - October 30, join builders around the world for a six-day online hackathon focused on creating ambitious AI applications with Runpod’s cloud infrastructure.

​Whether you’re building an inference API, AI agent, generative media workflow, fine-tuning pipeline, or an entirely new developer tool, this is your opportunity to turn an idea into a working project. Participants will have time to build remotely, connect with the Runpod team and community, and compete for cash prizes and platform credits.

​GPU-powered AI applications and workflows

Where Inference Meets Influence

The age of inference is here, and it’s time to connect infrastructure investment to enterprise ROI.

How is AI Infra Summit different from other AI events?

AI Infra Summit uniquely focuses at the infrastructure layer of AI. The show targets the crucial intersection of infrastructure and models that ultimately drives AI performance at the software layer. The agenda also focuses on serving AI at scale, and on deployment and operational challenges across the whole technology stack. 

There is no can-kicking or vague investigations of AI in XYZ industry here. AI Infra Summit is for the committed.

Who is AI Infra Summit designed for?

AI Infra Summit is a community of 8000+ pioneers focused on making AI faster, more efficient, more affordable, and more sustainable. We don't go deep into specific enterprise applications, but we knit together all of the various pieces of the infrastructure layer that keeps AI scaling. 

You could go to countless AI, datacenter, semiconductor or robotics conferences in a year and still not be able to piece everything together... Or you can come to just one.

 

What challenges in AI infrastructure does the summit focus on?

AI Data Centers, Compute, Data Movement, Data & Models and Physical AI. The bottom four layers of Jensen Huang's AI layer cake.

AI has a cost problem, an energy consumption problem and a scalability problem. All of these issues can be resolved at the infrastructure layer and this is the mission of AI Infra Summit. Ultimately, the quality of infrastructure will determine the viability of AI investment & growth, and the palatability of continuing AI development to the public.

About Event

​AI is moving faster than most security programs can keep up with — agentic tools, MCP servers, and AI-generated code are shipping into production every day, often outrunning the guardrails meant to protect them. This hackathon brings developers and security practitioners together to get hands-on with the skills defining the new discipline of AI Security Engineering. Working in teams, participants will tackle real-world AI security challenges spanning the OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications, threat modeling AI/agentic systems, securing MCP servers and agent skills against tool poisoning and supply-chain attacks, hardening vibe-coded applications, and red-teaming a live chatbot to find and exploit vulnerabilities before attackers do.

​Whether you're a developer curious about securing AI-powered apps or a security specialist looking to apply your skills to LLMs and agents, you'll leave with practical, portfolio-ready experience — and the kind of muscle memory that only comes from breaking (and fixing) real systems. No prior AI security experience required — just a builder's mindset and curiosity about where AI meets attack surface.

candidates.title: The Next Interface Hackathon: Rethink how we talk to AI
candidates.evidence:
The Next Interface Hackathon: Rethink how we talk to AI
For three years, using AI meant typing into a box and waiting for text to come back.
That era is ending. 

The next interface isn't a chat window. It's worn, spoken, and always on.
Glasses that listen.
A pendant that remembers. 
A tracker you never charge. 
A second self that watches your screen and acts before you ask.
We're putting the founders building that future in one room with the people who want to build on it.

Half a day in San Francisco. 

Real hardware on the table. Working demos, not slideware.
The lineup is a short list of founders shipping the wearables that are pulling AI off the screen. 

The founders in the room:
Adam Cohen Hillel, Secondly - a personal AI "second self" that sees your screen and acts across every app you use. The chat box becomes a presence.
Nik Shevchenko, Omi - the open-source AI wearable necklace, with 250+ developer apps already built on it. Always listening, always yours.
AnhPhu Nguyen, Mira - AI smart glasses with no camera. They hear what you hear, recall every name, and translate 60+ languages in under a second. AnhPhu is the Harvard builder behind last year's viral I-XRAY demo.
Andy Kong, Chargerless - a 7-gram health tracker powered by daylight. One minute of sun a day and it never needs a charger.
What you'll build: pick a device, an API, or a live sensor stream. 

Ship something a person could actually wear or talk to by the time we demo.

 The strongest builds demo to the founders in the room.
This is for builders, hardware hackers, AI engineers, and designers who think the keyboard is a temporary technology.
Leverage
Nir Naamani
Adam Cohen Hillel

What you'll build: pick a device, an API, or a live sensor stream. 

Ship something a person could actually wear or talk to by the time we demo.

 The strongest builds demo to the founders in the room.

About Event

​Car AI Navigation Hackathon

Challenge: We have a mini city road with lanes, intersection and traffic signs. Your job is to use AI and a small autonomous car like the Donkeycar or equivalent (typically 1/16th scale or smaller RC car with a Raspberry Pi or equivalent and a camera controlling it) to navigate the "city", obeying signs and making it from one side to the other in the fastest time. 

You must bring your own car, which should be ready to run, with compute and camera already onboard and working. The objective of the hackathon is to add AI "city" navigation to it.

You can use onboard AI, AI on your laptop via Wifi or AI in the cloud to help with the navigation. Think creatively about what kind of AI to use and what's the fastest way to do it!

This is not an event for spectators, nor will cars be provided to those who arrive without one. This is a hackathon, not a regular race. Come ready to hack!
